pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: packages/domain/src/resource.ts:161 When the probe cannot read CPU load, the admission gate admits the CPU-costly job and records nothing about the missing reading, so 'could not check' looks the same as 'checked and clean' to the operator, while an unread commit charge two conditions earlier (line 152) is refused out loud.

techniques.evidence: packages/domain/src/resource.ts:161 The admission gate sits in the work's path, so letting the actor through on a broken instrument is allowed, but only if it is loud to the operator on a code of its own. An unread cpuBusy is quietly treated as clean, and no waiting/unread event is written. An unread comfyQueue (line 164) gets the same silent pass, but profileReady refuses on it. The memory branch (line 152, refuse 'unread') does conform.
packages/kernel/src/resources/gate.ts:30 A probe that throws gives an empty MachineLoad, so memory-costly jobs wait as 'unread' and are never admitted on a reading of zero.
packages/domain/src/resource.ts:16 Admission charges peaks that the kernel's profiler measured, not a cost the producer declares. A profile job is never profiled itself (PROFILER, line 98).

pairs.registryProposal: The in-path split in unmeasurable-criteria (open to the actor, loud to the operator) covers runtime admission gates as well as CI gates. use_when could name 'a resource admission gate whose probe can come back partly unread' so that seats judging runtime gates find it.

techniques.evidence: tests/golden-path/step-record-literal-keys.probe.spec.ts:70 Two of the three remedies it names no longer exist: a repo-wide grep finds only unrelated private patchRecord helpers in lib/producers.

tests/golden-path/step-record-literal-keys.probe.spec.ts:15 The check knows a key passed through a const escapes it. On owned code it accepts that blind spot and does not refuse the unrecognised form.

lib/steps/withStore.ts:38 The close-what-you-open rule was taken out of a stale prose count and mechanised in a probe.
tests/golden-path/step-record-literal-keys.probe.spec.ts:55 The instrument is asserted before the result: a walk that found almost nothing fails instead of passing.
tests/golden-path/step-record-literal-keys.probe.spec.ts:17 The haystack is normalised to code, so a comment quoting the forbidden call neither counts nor hides.
tests/golden-path/shared-notebook-contracts.probe.spec.ts:184 Exemptions are keyed by file, must carry a reason, and fail once the file stops leaking (lines 186-190).
lib/steps/recordRegistry.ts:190 A future or malformed record gets a distinct 'refused' outcome, separate from both failed and never-written, and is never cast.

pairs.evidence: lib/foundry/scout/needs.ts:109 The stale-needs refusal tells the reader to run a command in a sibling checkout as the literal 'in pof', even though the module resolves that root itself (needsRoot: EXPORT_ROOT_POF or ../pof). The remedy is not printed where it would actually run.

techniques.evidence: lib/foundry/scout/needs.ts:109 The remedy lives outside the tree and is given as a literal, not resolved from needsRoot(). By contrast, doctor.ts:143 resolves COMFY_START from the environment.
lib/foundry/scout/doctor.ts:315 Which checks block is computed from the needed flag. Notes cannot fail the night.
lib/foundry/scout/doctor.ts:319 The printed FAIL/note tag comes from the same Check fields as blocking(), so the surface cannot understate what blocks.
lib/foundry/scout/doctor.ts:204 A condition that was not evaluated is shown as an explicit skip with its reason, not as ok. The judge also fails an unread age closed (muse.ts:81).
lib/foundry/scout/planDoors.ts:32 The plan-time rung reuses the launch door's own parser, so one check runs at both rungs.
lib/foundry/scout/planDoors.ts:37 Checks over the payload block at plan time. Checks that read the world (caps, money, seed state) are kept for launch, where their input is current.
lib/foundry/scout/budget.ts:16 The budget gate reads the kernel's meter rows, not a figure the gated night keeps for itself.
lib/foundry/scout/plan.ts:31 Queued plan items have an 'expired' terminal state when the night's until passes, so they cannot sit queued forever.
lib/foundry/scout/plan.ts:52 Each non-satisfied terminal state carries a reason from a closed state vocabulary; none is blank.
lib/foundry/scout/judge.ts:20 The eye has a separate 'will not say' token instead of being forced to invent an age, and that token fails closed in judgeFailure.
